findings.title: Cache key uses Python's `hash()` which is randomized per-process, making the cache ineffective across workers
findings.body: The cache key is built using `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. Since Python 3.3, `hash()` for strings and tuples is randomized per-process via PYTHONHASHSEED. In a multi-worker deployment (e.g., gunicorn, uwsgi), each worker will compute a different hash for the same project IDs, so cache entries written by one worker will never be found by another. This completely defeats the stated performance optimization goal. Use a deterministic hash like `hashlib.md5` or simply join the sorted IDs into a string key.

findings.title: Substring check for `event.type:error` matches negated queries, causing incorrect upsampling
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` checks `if "event.type:error" in query` using a naive substring match. A query like `!event.type:error` (which explicitly excludes errors) or `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` would still match this substring. This would incorrectly apply the `upsampled_count()` transformation to queries that include non-error events or exclude errors entirely, producing wrong counts. The check needs to be aware of negation and boolean operators, or at minimum verify the token is not preceded by `!`.

findings.title: Git submodule file accidentally committed at repository root
findings.body: A file named `sentry-repo` containing `Subproject commit a5d290951def...` was added at the repository root. This appears to be an accidentally committed git submodule reference (likely from running a command inside a nested clone). It will cause confusion for other developers and CI systems, and should be removed from the PR.

findings.title: Linear scan of allowlist for each project ID is O(n*m)
findings.body: `all(project_id in allowlist for project_id in project_ids)` performs a linear scan of the `allowlist` list for every project ID. If the allowlist grows large (hundreds or thousands of entries) and queries include many projects, this becomes O(n*m) per call. Since this is called on every stats request (before the cache check returns), converting `allowlist` to a `set` first would make each lookup O(1).

findings.title: `upsampled_count()` sums `sample_weight` but events without the field will silently produce undercounts
findings.body: The `upsampled_count` SnQL function computes `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`. In ClickHouse, `sum()` skips NULL values. If any event in an allowlisted project lacks a `sample_weight` value (e.g., events ingested before the feature was enabled, or events from SDKs that don't send `client_sample_rate`), those events will be silently excluded from the count rather than counted as 1. This produces an undercount without any indication to the user. A `COALESCE(sample_weight, 1)` or similar fallback would be safer.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility is checked against the outer `dataset` variable, not the `scoped_dataset` actually used for the query
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is called with the outer `dataset` (captured from the enclosing `get` method). However, when called via `get_event_stats_factory`, the `scoped_dataset` parameter can differ from `dataset` (e.g., when the dashboard widget split logic passes `discover` as `split_dataset` while the original `dataset` might be something else). This means the upsampling decision could be based on the wrong dataset, potentially applying or skipping the transform incorrectly.

findings.title: Integration tests mock `options` but not the cache, so cached results from one test may leak into another
findings.body: The test class mocks `sentry.api.helpers.error_upsampling.options` but does not clear or mock the cache used in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects`. If tests run in sequence and share the same cache backend, a cached eligibility result from one test (e.g., `test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects` caching `True`) could be returned in a subsequent test that expects a different result (e.g., `test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist`), causing flaky or incorrect test outcomes. The cache should be cleared in `setUp` or the cache layer should be mocked.
